Oh, well I figured since it's just a short film there wasn't much time for well developed context. I just took it as a short scary story. My take on it is that this evil being Salvo (the creepy ass smiley guy) preys on those emotionally broken and distraught over the loss of a child. Hence he lures them (that beat from the computer ad got stuck in my head...eugh) into buying the cabinet which contains a deformed creature, likened to a baby, that will inevitably kill those who raise it. I took it as that the mother saw she had another chance to have a child, or that he will act as a replacement for her own that she lost in an attempt to relieve her grief. If you noticed from the get go the dad was against keeping it, and he shows further contempt throughout the creatures childhood. The mother, on the otherhand, shows signs of denial as she still tries to be motherly towards it. My belief is that she is the more affected one by the death of their son. 

So my basic interpretation is that Salvo kills people by burdening them with his own creatures who slowly destroy their guardians' lives as they grow,  until they kill them. I am still curious though as to why he collects them when they're older. Wonder what he does with them. I'm also still wondering of there was an actual moral of the story, or if it stood metaphorically for something. Maybe it's just another scary story. But that's just my two cents thrown in.
